subject: Biotechnology
title: Approved Gene Therapies
description: A quick win: understand Approved Gene Therapies.

hook.text: Luxturna restores vision to people born with a rare retinal blindness — a single injection per eye.

buildup.text: Zolgensma treats spinal muscular atrophy in infants — the most expensive drug ever at $2.1 million per dose.

discovery.text: Casgevy is the first CRISPR therapy approved — editing patients' own stem cells to cure sickle cell disease.

twist.text: Gene therapies cost millions because patient populations are tiny — the economics of rare diseases challenge access.

climax.text: Over 20 gene therapies are now approved globally — the trickle has become a steady stream.

punchline.text: Gene therapy went from dream to prescription — the cures are here.

quiz.question: What is Casgevy notable for?
options: It is the first vaccine produced using gene therapy techniques
It is the first CRISPR-based therapy approved to treat sickle cell disease
It is the cheapest gene therapy available worldwide

details.summary: Over a dozen gene therapies have received regulatory approval worldwide, treating conditions from inherited blindness to spinal muscular atrophy and sickle cell disease.
details.whyItMatters: Approved gene therapies prove the technology can cure previously untreatable genetic diseases. Every new approval expands the evidence base and builds regulatory precedent, accelerating the path for hundreds more gene therapies currently in
takeaways: Luxturna restores vision in inherited retinal dystrophy caused by RPE65 mutations
Zolgensma provides a one-time treatment for spinal muscular atrophy in infants
Casgevy became the first approved CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease

faq.question: What was the first gene therapy approved in the Western world?
faq.answer: Glybera was approved in Europe in 2012 for familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency but was withdrawn due to extreme cost and tiny patient population. Luxturna, approved in the US in 2017 for inherited blindness, became the more impactful milestone as a commercially viable gene therapy.

faq.question: How many gene therapies are currently approved worldwide?
faq.answer: As of 2024, over 15 gene therapies are approved globally across the US, EU, and other markets. They treat conditions including inherited blindness, spinal muscular atrophy, hemophilia, sickle cell disease, and certain cancers. Hundreds more are in clinical trials.
